entry.title: Anthropic builds custom Scion source control system to handle surge from 2,500 to over 30,000 daily code merges in 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic redesigned its source control system, creating a custom tool called Scion to manage a dramatic increase in code changes, rising from about 2,500 merges per day in May 2026 to over 30,000 by September. The new system replaced Git to accommodate extreme scale, including a main branch history of nearly 100 GB and 25 million daily code checkouts for continuous integration and other environments. The migration to Scion was completed in five months by a team of seven engineers. Anthropic also developed a new code review system named Antique and uses adversarial review techniques involving AI models to improve code quality while avoiding over-engineering. The surge in coding activity correlates with the release of new AI models such as Fable and Mythos during 2026, which likely contributed to the increased development velocity.

entry.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Argon, a physical reasoning AI model advancing robotics control and simulation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Argon, a general-purpose AI model designed to enhance physical understanding, code generation, and visual-semantic reasoning for robotics. Argon achieved an 87% score on the Embodied Reasoning benchmark, outperforming other leading models in solving spatial problems in 3D environments. The model supports various robotics tasks including mobile manipulation, zero-shot control, simulation reconstruction, and self-improvement through iterative learning. Gemini 4 Argon enables robots like Boston Dynamics Spot to perform complex tasks such as manipulating objects and interacting with physical environments by creating digital twins and verifying actions through multi-agent systems.

entry.title: OpenAI engineer arrested for planting encrypted audio recorders in executive conference room at San Francisco headquarters [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: An OpenAI engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested and charged with using devices to intercept oral communications after audio recorders were found concealed in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco office. Federal prosecutors allege Alfozan, a Saudi national employed since July 2025, installed the devices to capture confidential meetings involving proprietary research and strategic information. OpenAI discovered the devices in late September and used its AI models to analyze the equipment and its data, then referred the case to the FBI. Surveillance footage and chatbot activity linked to Alfozan and his spouse indicated planning and technical knowledge related to building and encrypting recording devices. The FBI and U.S. attorney's office are prosecuting the case as a national security matter, with Alfozan facing up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine if convicted.

entry.title: DeepMind's Argon tool accelerates Chrome's architectural refactor, enabling live webpages to move between tabs and windows without reloading
entry.summary: DeepMind developed Argon to help the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a large legacy codebase within Chromium. This tool allowed multiple clean code changes simultaneously, completing months of architectural refactoring across hundreds of files in weeks. For Chrome's billions of users, this update will enable live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, reducing browser crashes.

entry.title: Developer reports AI bot traffic surge after posting on Hacker News, causing website slowdown and prompting infrastructure upgrades [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A developer who posted about their customizable feed reader on Hacker News experienced a significant increase in AI bot traffic to their website, which caused severe slowdowns. Investigation revealed that nearly half the traffic came from a single service that frequently queried the site to monitor changes and generate AI summaries, alongside other known crawlers and vulnerability scanners. In response, the developer implemented measures including blocking abusive bots, adding a robots.txt file to manage crawler access, and setting rate limits. They also undertook infrastructure improvements to enhance website performance and scalability, aiming to better handle high traffic volumes in the future.

entry.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 embedding model repurposed into a speech-to-text system running on MacBook Air with 5% word error rate [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers adapted Google's EmbeddingGemma 2, originally a multimodal embedding model for text, images, audio, and video, into a speech-to-text model that transcribes audio on-device in about 13 seconds per hour of audio on a base MacBook Air. The approach uses the original audio encoder and a small trained reader to map audio slices to text space, selecting the closest word from a large vocabulary and adding punctuation and capitalization with a tiny additional model. The reader model was trained for under two hours on English speech data, while the base model was not originally designed for transcription. The system achieves a word error rate of about 5%, compared to 2-3% for leading speech models, with plans to improve accuracy through better reader training. Users can transcribe audio files or dictate directly on Mac devices using the Neural Engine, ensuring audio data remains local.

entry.title: Character.ai files for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy to pursue court-supervised sale amid legal and operational challenges [ * ] [ ◻ ]

entry.title: Developer shares insights on building an AI harness for game development using Claude Code and LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A game developer presented a talk on using large language models (LLMs) like Claude Code to assist in game development, focusing on practical, day-to-day workflows rather than one-off demos. The developer discussed challenges with applying LLMs to traditional game projects, noting that games contain many non-code elements that are difficult for AI to handle compared to web-based software projects. The presentation highlighted the developer's experience starting with a web-based project called mood.site, which helped explore LLM capabilities in coding. They emphasized that while LLMs excel at generating web app code, their effectiveness in game development is limited by the complexity and opacity of game assets and systems. The talk aimed to share these insights more broadly beyond the conference audience.

entry.title: Pulse Local launches Mac budgeting app with AI models running entirely on users' machines to enhance privacy and performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Pulse Local is a budgeting app for Mac that processes AI queries locally on the user's device, keeping both financial data and questions private without sending information to cloud services. The app offers comprehensive budgeting features including plans, rules, cash flow, and forecasting, all operating offline to protect user privacy. The app supports multiple currencies and date formats for global users, with bank synchronization currently available for US banks via Plaid and CSV imports for others. Pulse Local is available as a free or paid app with optional bank sync subscription, and the developers plan to expand support to Windows and improve AI accuracy in future releases.

entry.title: Google DeepMind outlines safety and security measures for Gemini 4 Argon AI model with advanced misuse prevention and real-time misalignment monitoring [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google DeepMind has detailed its approach to developing the Gemini 4 Argon AI model responsibly, focusing on safety and security to prevent misuse and ensure alignment. The model, designed for complex tasks in coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science, includes advanced cyberdefense capabilities and has been tested through limited access programs like Fairwind to identify vulnerabilities and improve protections. The company implemented multiple layers of real-time safeguards, including input screening, internal introspection, and continuous monitoring, to prevent harmful uses such as cyberattacks or biological threats. Testing showed significant improvements in reducing harmful outputs and preventing jailbreak attempts. Additionally, DeepMind conducted misalignment tests to ensure the model does not pursue unintended goals, finding no evidence of covert harmful behavior during realistic scenarios. The rollout of Gemini 4 Argon is expanding alongside these safety programs to trusted cyber defenders.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma highlighted that these developments challenge traditional industry assumptions about software-hardware ties and game discovery, potentially making games more accessible and fostering player creativity. The initiative responds to recent community-driven efforts where games have been ported to platforms like Apple Silicon and web browsers, and where game code has been merged to create new experiences. Xbox Labs will develop tools and share insights with developers, though Microsoft has yet to comment on issues related to unauthorized use of its intellectual property in these mods.

The model is accessible to developers, enterprises, and consumers through the AI Studio, Gemini platform, and Google AI Ultra subscriptions, with pricing starting at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google teams have used Argon to accelerate software engineering projects, optimize business workflows, identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and advance research in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and life sciences. Notable achievements include speeding up codebase refactoring in Chrome, enhancing open-source quantum chemistry tools, and improving AI model inference speeds.

entry.title: Jevcrawl launches a web crawler for AI agents that selects relevant content without using large language models, offering faster and cheaper targeted crawling [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Jevcrawl is a new web crawler designed for AI agents that identifies answer-relevant pages and passages without involving large language models (LLMs) in the crawling process. It uses a small decision model to pick links and passages, reducing token usage and costs while improving speed and accuracy compared to LLM-driven crawlers. The crawler operates by scoring page content rather than generating text, ensuring safety against prompt injection and providing verbatim passages with source references. Benchmarks show Jevcrawl finds answer pages more frequently and at a fraction of the cost and time compared to alternatives like Crawl4AI. It integrates with various AI agent platforms and offers command-line tools for setup and use.

OpenAI Scrambles to Fix Safety Issues Before Shipping Its Next Flagship Model [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI is grappling with fallout from its use of a controversial innovation in AI design as it works to get its next unreleased model to a place where leaders believe they can safely release it. The model design, known as loop transformers or recurrent depth, can make it harder to monitor the way the AI "thinks," or how it reasons and processes its response to a question or task, The Information reported last month. That means the technique could erode a key tool that OpenAI and other companies rely on to catch misbehaving models. OpenAI hasn't publicly acknowledged the technique, but Microsoft last week accidentally confirmed OpenAI's use of it in one of the AI company's most advanced commercially available models, GPT-6.1 Sol, in a blog post it has since edited to remove the disclosure.

When the price doubles it will still be a little cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. (I used ChatGPT to edit that chart! entry.title: Rebuilding Companies for the Agentic Era [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Companies have spent the past few years figuring out how to put AI to work. In 2026, some are confronting a bigger question: What should a company look like when AI can understand context, coordinate work and act across systems? The Information's Co-Executive Editor Amir Efrati sat down with leaders from three companies at the forefront of this shift to discuss how agentic AI is changing how companies work and operate. Owen Jennings, Business Lead & Executive Officer, Block Stephanie Cohen, Chief Strategy Officer, Cloudflare Surabhi Gupta, CTO, Klaviyo Redesigning the operating model Block and Cloudflare offered two ways to rethink the operating model. For Cloudflare, Stephanie Cohen said the company had to rethink the work itself, not simply add AI tools onto existing processes. "If we didn't redesign how work was done, we weren't going to actually change what went on at Cloudflare," she said. "The only way for us to redesign the factory floor was to get rid of whole functions." At Block, the answer was to rebuild its functional model so engineering, product, design and sales teams work across Square, Cash App and Afterpay on shared capabilities. Owen Jennings said the change came about when AI agents became capable of writing production code in complex systems, prompting the company to ask how work should move when agents can share company context with humans. "We said, based on where the tools are now and based on where we think it's going, what functions do we need at the company? How do we want to organize?" recalled Jennings. The shift is showing up in customer experiences, with Square and Cash App surfacing tools, insights or actions at the right moment, rather than relying on static, one-size-fits-all surfaces. Block shipped about three times as many Square features in the first half of 2026 as a year earlier, he said. "There's a lot of conversation around automating things for the sake of it," said Jennings. "For us, it's about building useful stuff for customers." Humans still matter Companies leaning hardest into agents aren't necessarily trying to replace humans. Cloudflare hired 1,111 interns this year, including AI-native talent who Cohen said worked on "everything," including old-fashioned automation no one had made time to build. "By teaching them the company and allowing them to have access to our system, they've shown us a million ways that what we were doing didn't make sense," she said. Block has also built a workspace for working alongside agents. Buzz, an open source tool the company has released for people and AI agents, gives each agent its own identity, permissions and context. "The idea is not to remove people from the loop, but to make agent work visible and steerable so humans can focus on judgment, taste and customer understanding," Jennings said. Klaviyo wants engineers closer to customer outcomes rather than assigned tickets. "One of the things we've found very effective is having the engineers sit side-by-side with the partner functions, and have them become domain experts," said Klaviyo's Surabhi Gupta. Cloudflare runs hands-on workshops that are deliberately low-pressure, and names an AI "champion" on each team, typically someone already experimenting. "It's easier to ask a peer than to ask someone else who you feel like is not gonna understand why you don't know how to do everything," Cohen said. Companies also need infrastructure connecting agents to systems, data and context. Cohen described Cloudflare's approach as a "harness": a layer connecting AI models with security, systems of record, company context and employee identities, while letting the company switch models as needed. "Part of the problem is people started with the hammer and were like, 'here's this hammer, build this house.' The reality is you have to design the house," said Cohen. The new metrics Agentic AI is also creating new metrics to measure success. At Block, development velocity-the pace that new features are shipped-has become a key metric. Gupta says Klaviyo measures this too, as well as cost and hours saved as a result of agents. One metric no one on the panel could predict: headcount, though Cohen felt optimistic about growth. "My guess is we'll have more employees [in five years]," she said. "The human world is human-shaped, and humans want to interact with more humans."

entry.title: Why Companies Can't Prove Their AI Spending Pays Off [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The trillion-dollar question of the AI boom is whether businesses' spending on the technology pays off. But measuring that return is often uncertain, confusing or incomplete. That's because it takes time for AI to show a return on investment that can be demonstrated in a company's income statement, as we've written. A new study from the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School and GBK Collective, a consultancy, echoes this idea, showing that most companies are still tracking ROI by measuring whether it makes their workers more efficient rather than whether it is driving more revenue. The study, based on online surveys of 1,400 U.S.-based employees from firms that have at least 1,000 staff and generate more than $50 million annually, showed that 40% of managers measured AI's impact on their business in terms of "hours saved per employee" and 37% tracked how AI reduced their workers' errors. Only about 27% of managers said they track the revenue they generate from AI features, apps and tools they provide to their customers. Perhaps worryingly, 44% of managers said that over the next one to two years, AI's primary role will be to improve productivity and just 8% said it would be to drive new revenue or create new products.

entry.title: Neocloud Prime Intellect Acquires Startup To Speed Up Inference [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Neoclouds and so-called inference providers that help app developers run open source models are trying to differentiate themselves in a very crowded market. For instance, one such neocloud, Prime Intellect, which was valued at $1 billion in an equity financing in July, is buying a startup to help it make open models run faster and more cheaply on its Nvidia servers, compared to its rivals. Prime Intellect, based in San Francisco, is acquiring Moondream, a young developer of open-source models that has fewer than 10 employees, according to Prime Intellect co-founder and CEO Vincent Weisser. (Weisser wouldn't share the terms of the deal, but Moondream has raised $4.5 million in funding.) San Francisco- and Seattle-based Moondream is best known for an open-source vision-language model for analyzing and understanding images, like identifying boxes in an image of a warehouse or ads in a livestream. But Prime Intellect is largely acquiring the startup for its employees' skills in writing software to make models run more efficiently, Weisser said.

entry.title: Applied Intuition Fields Offers at $30 Billion Valuation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: For the last three years, AI labs like OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI have sucked up a lot of investor attention-as well as nosebleed valuations. Now a growing number of startups that make apps, agents or other software powered by AI are fetching valuations of $20 billion or higher. Applied Intuition, a maker of software to train self-driving vehicles, is slated to join this club. Applied Intuition has received investment offers that would value it at least $30 billion, according to people who have spoken to company leaders. The offers are likely to encourage the company to raise at least $1 billion in the next few months, they said.

entry.title: Applied And Lam Are Overlooked Chip Equipment Stocks
entry.summary: The AI chip sector has been picked clean of bargains, as stocks of chip designers, chip manufacturers and chip manufacturing equipment makers have all soared in the past year. But that doesn't mean there aren't still some opportunities if you know where to look. One example: Applied Materials, which makes machinery used in chip etching and deposition for memory chips-among the most highly sought-after components used in AI chips. As memory chip makers have quickly expanded manufacturing, companies like Applied and its nearest rival, Lam Research, have enjoyed surging demand for their products.

entry.title: Quoting Geoffrey Huntley [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: If the agent isn't using my diagnostics library, I could introspect and update AGENTS.md, but there's still a delta, and it'll drift. Instead, I write a pre-commit hook that checks the git diff for direct calls to observability modules that bypass my diagnostics module. Boom: fail the commit, inject a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library. All of a sudden it's ten out of ten. - Geoffrey Huntley, nobody should type code by hand anymore. here's what's left.
